PullRequest.Title: workbench: add frosted glass overlays with safe fallbacks
PullRequest.Body:
This adds theme-tinted frosted glass to desktop Editor and Agents overlays, while keeping solid backgrounds as the safe fallback for accessibility preferences and unsupported graphics.

### Changes

- Add `workbench.modernUIFrostedGlass` (enabled by default) and `workbench.modernUIFrostedGlassOpacity` (50-100%, default 92%). Editor windows require Modern UI; the Agents window uses its own modern presentation.
- Apply a shared material to quick input, context menus, dropdowns, hovers, custom dialogs, notifications, and action-list pickers, preserving the Agents window's existing surface colors.
- Respect OS and VS Code reduced transparency, high-contrast themes, forced colors, CSS support, and Electron GPU-compositing capability. Native OS menus/dialogs, web windows, editor backgrounds, and non-overlay panels remain unchanged.
- Keep blur on non-interactive paint layers and preserve whole-surface scale entrances without opacity flashes. Shared popup renderers cover plain, tabbed, and nested pickers in both windows, with stable anchoring, focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
- Migrate the former experimental setting names on desktop and report explicit choices through the existing configuration telemetry controls.
- Add regression coverage for capability changes, disposal/races, configuration and profile behavior, telemetry, theme restoration, and cross-window popup motion.

### Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` - passed with zero errors.
- Full Electron unit suite with CI locale (`en-US`) - 39,905 passing, 472 expected pending.
- Focused popup suites - 214 Electron and 213 Chromium tests passing.
- Configuration-isolation and capability regressions pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
- Client type-check, import-layer checks, scoped ESLint, stylelint, and commit hygiene - passed. Stylelint reports only existing design-token suggestions.
- Native macOS arm64, Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev - 23 recorded UI checks passed across Editor and Agents windows, including flat/tabbed model pickers, other dropdown families, submenu positioning, real blur during scale motion, and reduced-motion/transparency fallbacks.
- Physical Windows/Linux compositor and driver combinations still need manual validation.

### Before / after gallery

**21 matched comparisons: 10 Editor surfaces and 11 Agents surfaces.** Each image shows solid backgrounds on the left and frosted glass on the right.

These use the **same build and synthetic demo content**, with `workbench.modernUIFrostedGlass` disabled for Before and enabled for After. Most use **50% opacity** to make the material visible; the Command Palette and provider picker also show the **92% default**. Text/control opacity is unchanged.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed selectors and test coverage directly establish which surfaces receive the live filter, while the existing notification controller bounds but retains up to three settled toasts for 10-15 seconds (or indefinitely when sticky/hovered). Chromium must update a backdrop-filter result when pixels behind that surface change. Exact GPU time varies by driver, overlay area, and backdrop activity, so the severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: offscreen backdrop pixels and GPU blur/compositing passes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the filtered pixel area, the rate at which the editor/terminal behind it repaints, and the number of concurrently visible filtered overlays (up to three settled toasts, plus another popup surface).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: repeated GPU rendering work and potential dropped frames during otherwise smooth editor or terminal updates
Findings.PreviousBehavior: These surfaces used opaque theme backgrounds, so updates behind a notification or popup did not require capturing and blurring the backdrop.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Supported desktop Sessions windows, and Modern UI editor windows, now keep a live 12px backdrop filter on every selected visible overlay; settled notification surfaces retain that filter for their full visible lifetime.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 100 adds `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` to the shared `::before` layer selected for quick input, action widgets, hovers, dialogs, the notification center, and settled toasts (selectors at lines 84-91). The new setting defaults to enabled, and the contribution enables it automatically in Sessions windows once GPU compositing is reported.
Findings.Title: Avoid live blur on long-lived notification overlays
Findings.Impact: With the default glass setting in the Sessions window, a sticky notification or up to three ordinary toasts over an active terminal/editor can add repeated GPU filter work on every underlying frame, increasing GPU usage and causing dropped frames or battery drain for the entire toast lifetime.
Findings.Evidence: `frostedGlass.css` applies one live blur layer to the notification center and each settled toast, as well as other overlays. `NotificationsToasts.MAX_NOTIFICATIONS` is 3, normal purge time is 10-15 seconds, and sticky/hovered toasts are retained. These overlays sit over the editor/terminal, so typing, cursor animation, terminal output, or editor animation changes the sampled backdrop and causes repeated offscreen backdrop capture/filter/compositing for each visible surface. The GPU capability check only establishes hardware compositing; it does not eliminate this per-frame blur pass.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep long-lived notification center/toast surfaces solid, or gate their blur behind an explicit opt-in rather than the default glass class; retain glass only for short-lived modal popups whose backdrop is effectively static.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate frosted-glass capability after an Editor or Sessions workbench restores
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `FrostedGlassContribution` runs at `AfterRestored`; the workbench does not await capability detection, and only adding the glass class waits for the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Proxy `isGPUCompositingEnabled()` to the Electron main process, which synchronously reads `app.getGPUFeatureStatus()` there.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per enabled workbench window at post-restore activation, plus one after each disable/re-enable cycle; not one per container or overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No GPU capability IPC was issued for this feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the restore critical path; solid overlays remain usable while the request is pending.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One contribution per renderer/workbench window; auxiliary containers in the same renderer reuse the same result. A normal session has one or a few windows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one startup capability request per contribution. Separate renderer windows may request concurrently; request generations suppress stale responses.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The contribution retains `gpuCompositingEnabled` and an event listener while requested. Disabling clears that state; re-enabling performs one fresh query. There is no cross-window cache, but no per-overlay query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the proxy service and contribution call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: IPC duration and number of simultaneous windows vary, but the call count is tightly bounded and the main-process operation is local.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: a single post-restore local IPC per window is bounded and does not block workbench progress.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and update context menus, quick input, action-list pickers, and nested submenus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM construction and layout complete before entrance classes are added. Submenu opening and picker item refresh synchronously inspect active animations before geometry-dependent work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and animate compositor-backed popup surfaces containing a backdrop-filter paint layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filtered layer per visible popup or submenu; nested menus add one layer per level.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Popups used solid backgrounds; existing motion did not sample and blur the workbench backdrop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during popup presentation and can affect interaction frames.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Popup pixel area, menu nesting depth, number of item refreshes, and user popup-open frequency; normal operation has one root popup and a small submenu depth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM/layout work is serialized on the renderer thread. Visible CSS animations and filtered layers are composed concurrently by Chromium; there is no application-level queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The ordinary menu stylesheet node is reused globally, while shadow-root menus own a stylesheet. Completed entrance animations are no longer returned by `getAnimations`; no external data cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed rendering path and multiplicity; medium for whether transient use alone causes visible latency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transient popup cost depends on surface area and GPU/driver behavior; no trace establishes a separate threshold-crossing regression for short-lived popup motion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for transient popup motion or animation inspection; their frequency and duration are bounded, while the reportable unbounded-by-frame-duration case is the retained notification blur.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep notifications visible over an updating editor or terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Once a toast transition settles, or while the notification center is open, every underlying editor/terminal repaint must feed the visible backdrop-filter layer before the frame can be composed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture and apply a 12px GPU backdrop blur for each visible notification surface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three settled toast filters, or a notification-center filter, on each backdrop frame; frequency follows editor/terminal updates rather than notification changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opaque notification backgrounds did not require backdrop capture or blur when content behind them changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The filter passes are on the rendering path for every affected frame and can reduce frame throughput.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filtered pixel area multiplied by underlying repaint rate and visible filtered-surface count; the toast controller allows up to three settled toasts for 10-15 seconds, with sticky, focused, or hovered toasts lasting longer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to three toast blur layers are active together; other visible overlay layers can add further compositor passes. Chromium schedules these GPU passes without an application limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A live backdrop cannot be reused when sampled pixels behind it change. Solid-background fallback applies only when disabled, unsupported, reduced-transparency, high-contrast, or software-composited.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: selectors, default enablement in Sessions, toast lifetime/count, and live backdrop dependency are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact GPU milliseconds and affected hardware prevalence vary by overlay size, driver, and update rate.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported a medium rendering regression recommending solid or explicit-opt-in treatment for long-lived notification surfaces.

Scenarios.Scenario: React to configuration, theme, accessibility, auxiliary-window, and GPU-status changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Event handlers synchronously recompute settings and toggle one class/property per layout container; re-enabling then launches a capability IPC asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast GPU-info updates or GPU-process loss from Electron main to subscribed renderer windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per Electron GPU update/loss to each enabled workbench listener; not per container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No feature-specific GPU-compositing event crossed this IPC channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Class toggling occurs synchronously when the event arrives but scales only with the small container set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workbench containers, normally one plus a small number of auxiliary windows, and infrequent preference/theme/GPU events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Container updates are sequential. Request generations prevent stale asynchronous capability results from winning; GPU events apply immediately.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current opacity and capability are retained. Negative/disabled state is intentionally rechecked only after re-enable; there is no repeated query on opacity or theme changes while the listener remains installed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener ownership, request invalidation, and container loop are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Electron event frequency is platform-dependent, but these are lifecycle/capability events rather than frame-rate events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: lifecycle is cleaned up, stale requests are rejected, and work scales with a small bounded container count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Migrate legacy glass settings and report explicit configuration telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Migration is launched asynchronously by the existing configuration migration contribution; configuration telemetry runs synchronously when its contribution is constructed but iterates only configured keys.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist configuration updates generated by the two newly registered legacy-key migrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally two updates per present legacy value (remove old and add new), once per configured scope/override; zero when no legacy key exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two legacy keys were not migrated or rewritten.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The contribution does not await `migrateConfigurations` in its constructor, so persistence is off the immediate workbench critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect explicit application settings and enqueue classified configuration telemetry through existing appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per recognized explicit setting and scope; the two new settings add at most six events across application/user/workspace in the maximal test scenario, and zero for defaults.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Application keys were not traversed here, and these two glass-setting events did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous constructor work is bounded by configured application-key count and tiny event payloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two legacy setting keys across configured scopes/overrides and two new telemetry setting IDs across application, user, and workspace scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: For each populated migration target, old-key removal and optional new-key write are submitted concurrently through `updateValue`; folders are traversed by the existing migration service. Telemetry appender calls are synchronous per explicit value.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Migration is self-removing by clearing legacy keys, so successful work is one-time. Defaults produce no telemetry events; only explicit values are inspected and logged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for migration update multiplicity and telemetry enumeration; downstream storage/transport cost is bounded by the small payload count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender internals and unusual numbers of overrides vary, but realistic cardinality is small and migration is one-time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: both boundary paths are bounded, migrations become no-ops after success, and defaults do not emit events.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 35 changed files and every diff page. Reported one medium rendering regression: default live backdrop blur on long-lived notification overlays repeatedly consumes GPU work as content behind them updates. Startup IPC, capability/event lifecycle, popup animation inspection, configuration migration, and telemetry paths were traced and found bounded.
